quote: p24 'Gross of reinsurance £'000 / Estimate of cumulative claims' (columns 2010 & prior, 2011-2018, Total): One year later 613,297 562,504 481,417 498,673 603,846 723,929 995,089 [4,478,755]; Two years later 606,529 585,619 488,813 543,728 709,876 802,855 [3,737,420]; Three years later 606,383 570,063 478,734 561,213 719,226 [2,935,619]; Four years later 595,247 563,908 498,320 566,647 [2,224,122]; Five years later 591,137 569,744 495,139 [1,656,020]; Six years later 586,573 567,391 [1,153,964]; Seven years later 586,980 [586,980]; Eight years later 2,740,657 (2010 & prior); Estimated balance to pay ... 1,949,555. p24: 'Historic development includes a mix of prior year releases and deteriorations, and in 2018 gross and net deteriorations occurred.' p5: 'Strengthening of prior period reserves;'. p36 note 9 'Net claims outstanding' (adverse)/favourable run-off deviation 'Total (21,284) (24,829)'.

Latest diagonal (31 Dec 2018) minus previous (31 Dec 2017), underwriting years to 2016: 2011 586,980-586,573 = +407; 2012 567,391-569,744 = -2,353; 2013 495,139-498,320 = -3,181; 2014 566,647-561,213 = +5,434; 2015 719,226-709,876 = +9,350; 2016 802,855-723,929 = +78,926. Sum +88,583 GBP000 = +88.583m. 2010 & prior has only one printed cell (2,740,657), so it has no step; 2017 and 2018 are excluded. The filing states no gross prior-year amount in words: p5 gives no figure and p36 is net. So the triangle figure is the filing's figure. Difference from adopted 88.583 = 0.000, within tolerance max(0.5, 0.05x88.583 = 4.429).
basis_check: Gross. The table is headed 'Gross of reinsurance'. Its Estimated balance to pay total 1,949,555 equals gross claims outstanding at 31 December 2018 (p15 'Claims outstanding 24 1,949,555 1,547,219'). The companion 'Net of reinsurance' table totals 1,445,666 = 1,949,555 - 503,889 reinsurers' share (p14). The only prior-year amount given in words is the net run-off deviation (p36 note 9 'Net claims outstanding', total (21,284) adverse).
page_binding_check: Single-syndicate report. p24 running header 'CMA Syndicate 4444 Annual Report & Accounts 31 December 2018 Page 23 of 43'. The table includes the business of Syndicate 958, reinsured to close into 4444 with effect from 1 January 2018 (p17), which is now 4444's own. This syndicate's figure.
reasoning: The printed gross triangle reproduces the adopted +88.583m exactly, and the filing states no gross prior-year amount. The sign agrees with p24 ('gross and net deteriorations occurred') and with p5 ('Strengthening of prior period reserves'). The pack's stored grid drops the printed 'At end of underwriting year' row (357,761 ...) and labels the printed 'One year later' row as 'At end of underwriting', so its row labels are one year out. Each column's last two cells are still the printed end-2018 and end-2017 cells, so the estimator's steps are the right cells. Opening reserves of 1,547,219 are the gross balance 'At 1 January' before the RITC received during 2018 (p42 note 24; p15 2017 column).

takeon_triangle.evidence: Transfer in the report year: p17 'With effect from 1 January 2018 the 2015 year of account for Syndicate 958 has been reinsured to close (RITC’d) into Syndicate 4444. The financial statements include the RITC of syndicate 958, 2017 comparatives for syndicate 4444 are pre the RITC.' Amount: p42 note 24, gross provision for claims 'At 1 January 1,547,219 / Increase/ (decrease) in provision 56,883 / Foreign exchange 68,124 / RITC received 277,329 / At 31 December 1,949,555' (reinsurers' share RITC received 61,381). The p24 table does not say which column carries the 958 business. Its steps show the business is not in the end-2017 to end-2018 step. The whole 2011-2016 step is +88.6m, under a third of the GBP 277.3m of gross reserves taken on. The 2011-2015 steps are +0.4m, -2.4m, -3.2m, +5.4m and +9.4m. The only large step (2016, +78.9m) is smaller than the transfer. Business entering a column only at the end-2018 diagonal would add at least its reserves to that column's step, and p24 reports gross deteriorations, so there are no offsetting releases. Corroboration from outside this filing: syndicate_4444_2017.pdf p25 prints the same end-2017 diagonal a year earlier, at 31 Dec 2017 rates. Its figures are 2011 355,885; 2012 383,618; 2013 389,916; 2014 436,548; 2015 550,721; 2016 696,895. This filing prints 586,573; 569,744; 498,320; 561,213; 709,876; 723,929. So 2011-2015 were restated upward by 1.28-1.65 times to include the transferred business. 2016 moved 1.04 times, within the exchange-rate change (US$ 1.35 to 1.27, p36). The take-on sits in the restated earlier diagonals of 2011-2015, not in the step, and does not dominate the figure.

takeon_triangle.evidence: Transfer in the report year: p5 'With effect from 1 January 2023, Syndicate 1861's 2020 year of account closed into the 2021 year of account of Syndicate 4444 by way of a reinsurance to close transaction'. Amount: p45 note 25, gross provision for claims 'At 1 January 2,367,884 / RITC adjustment 313,953 / Adjusted 1 January 2,681,837 / Change in provision (68,651) / Foreign exchange (114,041) / At 31 December 2,499,145' (reinsurers' share RITC adjustment 147,677). So the earlier diagonals of 2019 and 2020 were restated to include 1861, and the take-on is not in the step.

takeon_triangle.evidence: Transfer: p4 '2011 was the final year of account for Syndicate 807, which then reinsured to close into the 2012 year of account of Syndicate 510.' p34: 'Syndicate 510’s profit commission is also subject to a deficit brought across as a result of the acceptance of the reinsurance to close of Syndicate 807’s 2011 and prior years of account'; years of account close 'normally at 36 months'. p117 (510 underwriting-year accounts): 'The reinsurance to close premium receivable includes £33,119,116 relating to the reinsurance to close for Syndicate 807, which reinsured into Syndicate 510’s 2012 year of account'. That table shows gross RITC premium receivable 491,194 and net 374,928; the basis of the GBP 33.1m is not stated. So the RITC took effect when 807's 2011 year of account closed at 36 months, at the 2013/2014 year end, into the 2012 year of account. The 2014 annual accounts (pp38-59) show no transfer line; 807 appears only as a run-off segment (p43 'Syndicate 807 run-off (414) (414) 2,263 (235) 285 1,899 22,138'; p51 gross 34,314, net 22,138). p11 says of 807: 'Favourable claims development on prior years led to this book contributing £2.2m to the overall underwriting profit of Syndicate 510.' Restatement: p44 says the table 'includes the historical development of Syndicate 807', so the earlier diagonals carry 807. Beyond tying 807 to the 2012 year of account, the note does not name the column. No step shows a take-on: 2012 -16.0, 2011 -11.3, 2010 +0.3, 2009 -4.4, 2008 & prior -17.0, where a GBP 33.1m take-on would show as a positive jump. The take-on does not enter the step and does not dominate the figure.

arithmetic: End-2019 minus end-2018 diagonal, pure years of account to 2017: 2011 122,781-118,862 = +3,919; 2012 73,737-76,959 = -3,222; 2013 80,173-89,044 = -8,871; 2014 127,787-131,492 = -3,705; 2015 127,367-128,197 = -830; 2016 193,887-201,210 = -7,323; 2017 278,512-252,295 = +26,217. basis_check: The table is headed 'Gross insurance contract outstanding claims provision as at 31 December 2019'. Its 'Claims outstanding per balance sheet' total of 515,336 equals gross claims outstanding (p19). The net table on p46 totals 229,301, the net closing balance (p34). The GBP 2.1m prior accident year development (p6, p33) is given without a basis. On p6 it sits in the paragraph on the claims ratio, which p6 defines as 'net claims incurred, as a percentage of net earned premiums'. On p33 the sentences before it give gross and net amounts for named losses, but this sentence gives one amount. For comparison, the net pure-year triangle gives +2.943m (1,116-801-2,027-2,007-316-1,011+7,989). No gross prior-year amount is stated.
page_binding_check: Single-syndicate report ('SYNDICATE 5151 ANNUAL REPORT AND ACCOUNTS', Endurance at Lloyd's Limited). p45 is note 24 of Syndicate 5151's financial statements. This syndicate's figure.
reasoning: Under the protocol, only an explicit gross statement overrides the triangle. The filing states GBP 2.1m of unfavourable prior accident year development twice (p6, p33), both times without a basis, and its context points to net (the net claims ratio paragraph). The printed gross table recomputes to +6.185m, equal to the adopted figure, with the same sign as the GBP 2.1m. The model's worry about RITC distortion finds no support: the filing's only RITC text is the accounting policy (p23), and the table reconciles to the balance sheet. The verdict rests on the GBP 2.1m not being a gross statement. A reader who treated it as gross would score a magnitude error (6.185 against 2.1). Opening reserves: p34 note 16, gross 'At 1 January 485,209 (267,307) 217,902'; p19 2018 column 485,209.
